Rashi on Gittin 13b:1:1.hebrew: לא שנא במלוה - ואע"ג דלהוצאה ניתנה ואינה בעין, הלכך לא בעינן צבורין, אי במעמד שלשתן קמיירי המתני':
Rashi on Gittin 13b:1:1.english: It is no different with a loan - Even though it was given to be spent and is not [physically] present, therefore we do not require [the money to be] piled, if the mishna is speaking of [a transfer] in the presence of all three [parties].

Rashi on Gittin 13b:3:1.hebrew: טעמא דמת - הוא דלא יתנו, דאין גט לאחר מיתה:
Rashi on Gittin 13b:3:1.english: The reason is that he died - That is [the reason] they should not give [it], for there is no divorce after death.

Rashi on Gittin 13b:3:2.hebrew: הא מחיים נותנין - ולא צריך תו לאימלוכי ביה:
Rashi on Gittin 13b:3:2.english: But [if he said it] while alive, they give [the get] - And there is no further need to deliberate about it.

Rashi on Gittin 13b:3:3.hebrew: וטעמא דאמר תנו - כלומר, והא דדייקינן "הא מחיים נותנין" — טעמא דאמר מעיקרא "תנו", כדקתני "תנו גט לאשתי":
Rashi on Gittin 13b:3:3.english: And the reason is that he said "Give" - That is to say, when we inferred, "But if [he died] during his lifetime, they give [the document]" — the reason is that he said at the outset "Give," as [the Mishnah] teaches: "Give a bill of divorce to my wife."

Rashi on Gittin 13b:3:4.hebrew: הא לא אמר תנו - אלא אמר כתבו, לא הוי. תלי תנא דמתני' טעמא דלא יתנו משום מיתה, דאפילו מחיים נמי אין נותנין עד דלימא תנו. מדלא קתני "האומר כתבו גט (זה) לאשתי ומת, לא יתנו לאחר מיתה", ש"מ דאי אמר הכי, אפילו מחיים נמי לא יהבינן. ואי בשכיב מרע, אע"ג דלא אמר תנו אלא כתבו, יהבינן, כרבי שמעון שזורי:
Rashi on Gittin 13b:3:4.english: But he did not say "Give" - but [rather] said "Write," it is not [valid]. The Tanna of the Mishnah attributes the reason [that] "they should not give" [the get] to death, [whereas] even during his lifetime they do not give it until he says "Give." Since it does not teach: "One who says, 'Write this get for my wife,' and died, they should not give it after death," learn from this that if he said this, even during his lifetime we would not give it. And if [the case is] a deathbed [sick person], although he did not say "Give" but [only] "Write," we give it, in accordance with Rabbi Shimon Shezuri:

Rashi on Gittin 13b:4:1.english: One who goes out in a neck chain - To be executed.

Rashi on Gittin 13b:4:2.hebrew: ואמר כתבו גט לאשתי - כדי שלא תזקק ליבם:
Rashi on Gittin 13b:4:2.english: And he said: Write a bill of divorce for my wife - So that she will not be bound to a levir:

Rashi on Gittin 13b:4:3.hebrew: הרי אלו יכתבו ויתנו - דמתוך שהוא בהול על נפשו, לא גמר למילתי'. ומיהו, מכל מקום "כתבו ותנו" הוה דעתיה:
Rashi on Gittin 13b:4:3.english: These should write and give - For since he is panicked about his life, he did not complete his statement. But nevertheless, [by saying] "write," his intention was [also] "and give."

Tosafot on Gittin 13b:1:1.hebrew: קסבר רב פפא כי אמר רב לא שנא מלוה לא שנא פקדון - וא"ת: ולרב פפא, ורב גופיה אמאי לא אוקי מתני' במעמד שלשתן, ואפי' אין צבורין? וכי תימא: משום דלא משמע ליה לישנא דמתני' במעמד שלשתן — אם כן, מהאי טעמא הוה ליה למימר דרב פפא לא אמר כרב זביד. וי"ל: אע"ג דמתני' לא משמע ליה לרב במעמד ג', מ"מ מדאתא רב פפא לאיפלוגי ארב זביד, משמע שיש לו כח וטעם, דבשום ענין לא מפרשא מילתא דרב משום מעמד שלשתן:
Tosafot on Gittin 13b:1:1.english: "Rav Pappa holds that when Rav spoke, there is no difference between a loan and a deposit" - And if you ask: [According to] Rav Pappa, why did Rav himself not establish the Mishnah as [speaking of a transfer] in the presence of all three parties, even if the coins are not piled? And if you say [it is] because the wording of the Mishnah does not imply to him [a case of] "in the presence of the three of them" — if so, for this same reason Rav Pappa should have said that he does not speak in accordance with Rav Zevid. And one can answer: Although the Mishnah does not imply to Rav [a case of] the presence of three, nevertheless, since Rav Pappa came to disagree with Rav Zevid, it implies that he has a strong basis and reasoning, [namely] that in no way is the statement of Rav explained on account of [the principle of] presence of the three of them:

Tosafot on Gittin 13b:2:1.hebrew: ממאי מדקתני תנו ולא קתני כתבו - וא"ת: הא דקתני "תנו", אשמעי' דאפי' הכי אין כופין את היורשים לשחרר, כרבי דפליג בירושלמי אדרבנן, ואמר דתנו לא הוי כשיחררו אלא ככתבו, ואין כופין. וי"ל דמתני' לא אתא לאשמועינן בדין מצוה לקיים דברי המת אם כופין היורשים לקיים אם לאו, אלא לאשמועי' דאין גט לאחר מיתה. ועוד דמסתמא כרבנן אתיא:
Tosafot on Gittin 13b:2:1.english: "From where?" From the fact that it teaches "give" and does not teach "write" - And if you ask: [Perhaps] by teaching "give," it informs us that even so, the heirs are not compelled to free [the slave] — in accordance with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who disagrees with the Rabbis in the Yerushalmi, and says that "give" is not like "free him" but like "write," and [so] they are not compelled. And one can answer: The mishna did not come to teach us, regarding the law of the obligation to fulfill the words of the deceased, whether the heirs are compelled to fulfill [them] or not, but rather to teach us that there is no bill of divorce after death. Moreover, [the mishna] presumably follows the Rabbis:
